bio.en: The first woman to hold a full professorship in mathematics (Stockholm); known for the Cauchy–Kovalevskaya theorem.
Wife of Menelik II who founded Addis Ababa and commanded troops at Adwa, where Ethiopia routed the Italians.
His reign (1867–1912) saw the Meiji Restoration and Japan's rapid modernization.
Dutch Post-Impressionist painter of Sunflowers and The Starry Night, who sold almost nothing in his lifetime.

role.en: poet and hero of Cuban independence

bio.en: A poet whose verses became the song 'Guantanamera' and organiser of Cuba's war of independence; he was killed in one of its first battles.
Abolished slavery, carried out Western-style reforms and kept Siam the only Southeast Asian country never colonised.
Created the philosophy of all-unity: the world strives for union with God through love and humanity towards "Godmanhood". He hoped to reunite the churches and inspired Silver Age poets.
An outlaw who made his last stand against police in home-made steel armour; to many Australians a symbol of defiance against unjust authority.
Viennese physician who founded psychoanalysis and the theory of the unconscious; author of The Interpretation of Dreams.
Serbian-American inventor of the induction motor and alternating-current systems, and a pioneer of radio.

role.en: 28th US president, World War I and the League of Nations

bio.en: He took the US into World War I in 1917 and set out the Fourteen Points for the postwar order. He won the creation of the League of Nations and the Nobel Peace Prize for 1919, but the Senate refused to ratify the Treaty of Versailles.
A Kaluga schoolteacher who showed that spaceflight was possible with rockets and derived the rocket equation.
Theodore Roosevelt's successor, who pursued "dollar diplomacy" in Latin America and China. He is the only person to have been both president and Chief Justice of the United States (1921–1930).

Showed that language is a system of signs in which a word's meaning comes from its difference from other words. His Course in General Linguistics, published from students' notes in 1916 after his death, became the basis of structuralism.

role.en: 26th US president, the Panama Canal and trust-busting

bio.en: The youngest US president, taking office at 42. He broke up monopolies, created national parks, began the Panama Canal and won the Nobel Peace Prize for mediating the Russo-Japanese War (1906).

He urged a return "to the things themselves": describing experience as it is given to consciousness, setting theories aside. Heidegger's teacher; under the Nazis he was barred from the university because of his Jewish origins.
Master of the short story and author of The Seagull, Three Sisters and The Cherry Orchard; a physician by training.
Bengali poet, writer and composer; the first non-European Nobel laureate in Literature (1913).

role.en: writer, national hero of the Philippines

bio.en: Filipino writer and physician, author of Noli Me Tángere; executed by Spanish authorities and honoured as a national hero.
The first Australian to win world operatic fame; peach Melba and Melba toast were named after her.

He came to the throne on the eve of defeat in World War I and cooperated with the Entente powers occupying Istanbul. After the sultanate was abolished in November 1922 he left on a British warship and died in exile in Sanremo.

role.en: industrialist, founder of Ford Motor Company

bio.en: Founder of the Ford Motor Company who introduced the moving assembly line and made the car a mass product with the Model T.
Disciple of Ramakrishna who introduced Vedanta and yoga to the West, famed for his 1893 Parliament of Religions speech.

role.en: First World War king who founded the House of Windsor

bio.en: He reigned through the First World War and in 1917 changed the royal house's German name to Windsor. A first cousin of Nicholas II and Wilhelm II, in 1932 he gave the first royal Christmas broadcast on radio.
He won in 1920 promising a "return to normalcy" after the war. His administration is remembered for the Teapot Dome scandal; he died in office in San Francisco in 1923.

role.en: revolutionary, founding father of the ROC

bio.en: Founder of the Kuomintang and leading figure of the 1911 Xinhai Revolution that ended imperial rule in China.

role.en: physicist and chemist, twice Nobel laureate

bio.en: Pioneer of radioactivity who discovered polonium and radium; the first woman Nobel laureate and the only person to win in two sciences.

role.en: last Russian emperor, executed with his family

bio.en: His reign saw the 1905 Revolution, the creation of the State Duma and Russia's entry into the First World War. He abdicated in 1917 and in 1918 was shot with his family by the Bolsheviks in Yekaterinburg.

role.en: leader of the Indian independence movement

bio.en: Leader of India's independence struggle and pioneer of nonviolent resistance (satyagraha).

role.en: revolutionary, head of the Soviet government

bio.en: Leader of the Bolsheviks who led the October Revolution of 1917 and headed the Soviet government until his death.

role.en: Japanese philosopher, founder of the Kyoto School

bio.en: A professor at Kyoto University who brought Zen experience together with Western philosophy. In An Inquiry into the Good (1911) he made "pure experience" his central idea.

role.en: physicist who discovered the atomic nucleus

bio.en: A New Zealander who discovered the atomic nucleus and first split the atom; 1908 Nobel laureate in chemistry and mentor to a generation of physicists.
Norwegian who led the first expedition to reach the South Pole (1911) and first sailed the Northwest Passage.

role.en: 30th US president, "Silent Cal" and the Roaring Twenties

bio.en: A taciturn Republican who presided over the boom of the Roaring Twenties. He cut taxes and limited government intervention; under him all Native Americans received US citizenship (1924).

role.en: British philosopher, logician and public intellectual

bio.en: A founder of analytic philosophy who tried to derive mathematics from logic (Principia Mathematica, with Whitehead) and clarify philosophical problems through the analysis of language. Nobel Prize in Literature (1950); anti-nuclear campaigner.
In 1906 in Paris he made the first publicly witnessed aeroplane flight; Brazilians regard him as the inventor of the aeroplane.

role.en: Prime Minister of the United Kingdom

bio.en: British prime minister during the Second World War (1940–1945) and again in 1951–1955; Nobel laureate in Literature.

role.en: 31st US president, the 1929 crash and the Great Depression

bio.en: A mining engineer who led food relief for Belgium in World War I and for famine-stricken Soviet Russia (the ARA, 1921–1923). Seven months into his term the stock market crashed and the Great Depression began.

Philosopher of freedom and creativity: freedom precedes being, and humans are called to creation as a continuation of God's work. Expelled from Soviet Russia in 1922 on the "Philosophers' ships", he lived in France.
Alsatian theologian, organist and doctor who founded a hospital at Lambaréné, Gabon; Nobel Peace laureate (1952).
Led the Soviet Union from the late 1920s until 1953, through industrialization, mass repression and the Second World War.
Developed the special and general theories of relativity; Nobel laureate (1921) for explaining the photoelectric effect.
A leader of the October Revolution of 1917 and founder of the Red Army. He lost the power struggle to Stalin, was expelled from the USSR in 1929 and was murdered in Mexico by an NKVD agent in 1940.
Under the slogan 'land to those who work it' he raised the peasants of southern Mexico; killed in an ambush, he became a symbol of agrarian justice.
A Javanese aristocrat whose letters on women's right to education, published after her early death, made her a national heroine of Indonesia.

role.en: ailing emperor of the 'Taishō democracy' era

bio.en: Meiji's son, reigned 1912–1926. Weakened by a childhood illness, he took little part in affairs; under him Japan fought in the First World War on the Entente side and parties and parliament grew stronger, and from 1921 his son Hirohito served as regent.
Spanish artist based in France, co-founder of Cubism and creator of Les Demoiselles d'Avignon and Guernica.
Founder of modern Chinese literature, author of 'A Madman's Diary' and 'The True Story of Ah Q'.

role.en: founder and first President of Turkey

bio.en: Led the Turkish War of Independence, proclaimed the Republic of Turkey in 1923 and carried out secularizing reforms.
The only US president elected four times; launched the New Deal in the Depression and led the country in World War II.
Australian geologist who led the Australasian Antarctic Expedition (1911–1914), mapping large areas of Antarctica.

role.en: German philosopher, founder of the Vienna Circle

bio.en: A professor at the University of Vienna around whom the Vienna Circle of philosophers and scientists gathered from 1924. In 1936 he was shot dead by a former student on the university staircase.
German-language writer from Prague, author of The Metamorphosis, The Trial and The Castle, mostly published posthumously.

role.en: 33rd US president, the atomic bombs and the start of the Cold War

bio.en: He succeeded Franklin Roosevelt in April 1945 and ordered the atomic bombings of Hiroshima and Nagasaki. He proclaimed the Truman Doctrine, backed the Marshall Plan and NATO, and entered the Korean War.
Largely self-taught Indian mathematician who produced thousands of results in number theory; worked with Hardy at Cambridge.

role.en: last emperor of Austria-Hungary, who tried to make a separate peace

bio.en: Grand-nephew of Franz Joseph, he came to the throne in 1916. He secretly sought a separate peace through his brother-in-law Sixtus of Bourbon-Parma, withdrew from government in November 1918, twice tried to regain the Hungarian throne and died in exile on Madeira; he was beatified in 2004.
Discovered the Raman effect in light scattering; the first Asian Nobel laureate in physics (1930).
A New Zealand writer who renewed the short story; she was compared with Chekhov, whom she regarded as her master.
One of the leading poets of Russia's Silver Age, author of Requiem and Poem Without a Hero.
Leader of the Nazi Party who ruled Germany in 1933–1945, started the Second World War in Europe and was responsible for the Holocaust.
Silent-film star who created the Tramp; made The Gold Rush, City Lights and Modern Times.
Independence leader and India's prime minister from 1947 until his death; a founder of the Non-Aligned Movement.
A Chilean teacher and poet who in 1945 became the first Latin American to win the Nobel Prize in Literature.

Saw philosophical problems as confusions of language: in the Tractatus, "whereof one cannot speak, thereof one must be silent"; in his later work, the meaning of a word is its use. Taught at Cambridge.

In Being and Time he returned philosophy to the question of the meaning of being, analysing finite human existence oriented towards death. Shaped existentialism and hermeneutics; his NSDAP membership in 1933–1945 remains debated.
Leader of the Vietnamese independence movement who declared independence in 1945 and led North Vietnam.

role.en: 34th US president, commander of the Normandy landings

bio.en: Supreme Allied Commander in Europe in World War II. As president he ended the Korean War (1953), built the Interstate Highway System, created NASA and warned against the "military–industrial complex".
Author of The Master and Margarita, Heart of a Dog and the play The Days of the Turbins.
Ethiopia's last emperor (1930–1974); led resistance to Italian occupation and helped found the Organisation of African Unity.

role.en: Chairman of the CCP, founder of the PRC

bio.en: Leader of the Chinese Communist Party who proclaimed the People's Republic in 1949 and led it until 1976.

role.en: Soviet leader who denounced Stalin's personality cult

bio.en: First Secretary of the Communist Party. His 1956 Secret Speech at the 20th Congress denounced Stalin and began the Thaw; his era saw Sputnik, Gagarin's flight and the Cuban Missile Crisis. He was ousted in 1964.

role.en: Second World War king who overcame a stammer

bio.en: He unexpectedly became king after his brother Edward VIII abdicated in 1936. He stayed in London through the Blitz, becoming a symbol of national resolve in the Second World War, and was the last Emperor of India.
First woman to fly solo across the Atlantic (1932); disappeared over the Pacific attempting to fly around the world.
Born in Kyiv, one of Israel's founders and its prime minister from 1969 to 1974.
Egyptian singer, one of the most celebrated performers of the 20th-century Arab world.

role.en: pharmacologist who made penicillin a drug

bio.en: An Australian who, with Ernst Chain, turned Fleming's discovery into a usable drug and got it into production during WWII; Nobel Prize 1945.
An Argentine master of labyrinthine stories about infinite libraries and mirrors; he directed the National Library after going blind.
Ruled Tonga for nearly half a century and kept it independent; the world took to her at Elizabeth II's coronation, riding through the rain in an open carriage.
Creator of Mickey Mouse and producer of Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs (1937); founded the Disneyland park.
Trumpeter and singer from New Orleans, one of the most influential figures in the history of jazz.
Proclaimed Indonesia's independence in 1945 and hosted the 1955 Bandung Conference that gave rise to the Non-Aligned Movement.

role.en: WWII-era emperor who announced Japan's surrender

bio.en: Reigned 1926–1989, longer than any Japanese monarch with reliable dates. Japan fought in China and the Pacific under him; on 15 August 1945 he announced the surrender by radio, and in 1946 he renounced his divinity to become a symbol of the state.
Turkish poet and playwright who renewed Turkish verse; spent years in prison and his last years in Moscow.
Arrernte artist famous for his watercolour landscapes of Central Australia.

Proposed falsifiability as the mark of science: a theory is scientific if experience could in principle refute it. In The Open Society and Its Enemies he criticised Plato, Hegel and Marx as sources of totalitarianism.
Chilean poet of Twenty Love Poems and the Canto General; Nobel Prize 1971. He died 12 days after Pinochet's coup.

The leading voice of existentialism: "existence precedes essence"; a person first exists and then makes themselves through choices they are responsible for. He declined the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1964.
One of the major composers of the 20th century, author of 15 symphonies including the Seventh, 'Leningrad', written during the siege.
A poet and co-founder of the Négritude movement, president of Senegal for 20 years and the first African elected to the Académie française.

role.en: Soviet leader of the Era of Stagnation

bio.en: He led the USSR for eighteen years — a time of stability and détente with the West, but also of economic stagnation, the crushing of the Prague Spring in 1968 and the invasion of Afghanistan in 1979.

Studied the nature of power and freedom; The Origins of Totalitarianism traced what Nazism and Stalinism shared, and her report on the Eichmann trial coined "the banality of evil". She fled Germany in 1933.
Led the development of the R-7 rocket, Sputnik (1957) and the Vostok spacecraft that carried Gagarin into orbit.
Mexican painter famous for her self-portraits and imagery drawn from Mexican folk culture.
Predicted the meson as the carrier of the nuclear force; Japan's first Nobel laureate (1949).
Australian cricketer widely regarded as the greatest batsman in the history of the game.

role.en: 36th US president, civil rights and the Vietnam War

bio.en: He succeeded the assassinated Kennedy and passed the Civil Rights Act (1964), the Voting Rights Act (1965) and the Great Society programs, while sharply escalating the Vietnam War.
Existentialist philosopher whose The Second Sex (1949) showed how society makes woman the "Other": "One is not born, but rather becomes, a woman". It became a founding text of second-wave feminism.
Applied structural linguistics to myths, kinship and customs: behind their diversity he looked for universal structures of the human mind. In the 1930s he studied Indigenous peoples of Brazil.
Led Ghana to independence in 1957, the first in sub-Saharan Africa, and championed Pan-Africanism.
Japanese director of Rashomon, Seven Samurai and Dersu Uzala, the last made in the Soviet Union.

role.en: nun, founder of the Missionaries of Charity

bio.en: Founded the Missionaries of Charity in Kolkata to serve the poor and sick; Nobel Peace laureate (1979).
Egyptian novelist, author of the Cairo Trilogy; the first Arabic-language Nobel laureate in Literature (1988).

role.en: ailing Soviet leader who ruled for thirteen months

bio.en: A Brezhnev loyalist chosen as General Secretary while already gravely ill. During his thirteen months in office the USSR boycotted the Los Angeles Olympics; his death opened the way for Gorbachev.

role.en: 40th US president, "Reaganomics" and the end of the Cold War

bio.en: A former Hollywood actor and governor of California. He cut taxes, built up arms and called the USSR an "evil empire", then signed the Intermediate-Range Nuclear Forces Treaty with Gorbachev (1987).
Devised the Turing machine, the basis of computation theory, and helped break the German Enigma cipher in the war.

role.en: 37th US president, the opening to China and Watergate

bio.en: He visited China in 1972, signed the SALT I treaty with the USSR and withdrew US troops from Vietnam. The Watergate scandal made him in 1974 the only US president to resign.

role.en: 38th US president, the pardon of Nixon

bio.en: The only president never elected as either president or vice president, appointed vice president and elevated by Nixon's resignation. He pardoned Nixon and signed the Helsinki Final Act (1975).
Born in Algeria. Author of The Stranger and The Myth of Sisyphus: the world is absurd, yet one can live in it honestly and revolt against meaninglessness. Nobel Prize in Literature, 1957.

As a student in Paris he and Léopold Senghor launched Négritude, a movement asserting the dignity and identity of Black peoples. Author of Notebook of a Return to the Native Land, he was mayor of Fort-de-France for over half a century.
